newsitem.title: ITALY: Pensions hard to touch in Italy budget - minister.
newsitem.headline: Pensions hard to touch in Italy budget - minister.

text.p: The Italian government will find it difficult to incorporate any revisions to pension reforms in its 1997 budget, while cuts are being studied in other sectors, said the Prime Minister's undersecretary Enrico Micheli.

"Intervening on the large areas of expendiutre will be difficult, and on the pensions in particular, because to go back and change after just a year after reforms were made will subject citizens to too sharp a shock," Micheli said in an interview with newspaper Il Messaggero.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government must present its 1997 financial budget to parliament by the end of September and the package must pass into law by year-end.

The package is set to deliver tough measures to show the nation's commitment to joining the European single currency in 1999 and aimed at cutting Italy's public sector borrowing requirement by 32.4 trillion lire.
The two largest areas of expenditure are pensions and public healthcare. Talks between ministers on the budget are set to start Tuesday.
Asked about cuts in the healthcare budget, Micheli replied that the government is still only in initial preparation over the financial budget.
